```markdown
### borrow_list
- Per-seat value VECTOR + np.roll rotation on backup, and np.roll(-curPlayer) on the training targets — cestpasphoto MCTS.py:175-183 and Coach.py:76-82. The minimal correct change that turns 2-player AlphaZero into n-player AlphaZero, and our only hook for 1v2 and 2v2 rewards.
- Seeded-universe determinization (PC-PIMC): a fixed table of magic seeds, one per universe, cycled per simulation on a SHARED tree — cestpasphoto MCTS.py:14,63 + SplendorLogicNumba.py:306-336. Cheaper and lower-variance than K independent whole searches. Our version samples deck order AND opponents' hidden deck-reserves from the publicly-known unseen multiset.
- same_player flag on every tree edge, negating the backup value only when the turn actually changes hands — Splendor-Zero native_mcts.cpp:54, 2470-2481. Required because our CHOOSE_TILE is a second decision node for the SAME acting seat.
- Playout Cap Randomization wired end to end: 25% of moves at n=48 WITH Gumbel root exploration and recorded; 75% at n=12 with argmax and NOT recorded — Splendor-Zero nn/selfplay_dataset.py:57-90 and cestpasphoto Coach.py:65-69. ~3x more games per unit compute at equal target quality.
- Forced playouts + policy-target pruning, k=0.5-2.0: during search force a child if Nsa < sqrt(k*P*N); at the root subtract the forced visits from the exported target and zero anything <=1 — cestpasphoto MCTS.py:75-80, 218-220; Splendor-Zero native_mcts.cpp:394, 1212. Six lines; prevents policy collapse without touching the network.
- Blended value target z = 0.5*(root value estimate) + 0.5*(game outcome) — Splendor-Zero nn/value_targets.py:12. One line, large variance reduction.
- Additive mask INSIDE the graph: append the 65-bool legal mask as a second network input, apply torch.where(mask, logits, -1e9) before log_softmax, and export it that way — cestpasphoto SplendorNNet.py:404 and davidADSP/SIMPLE models/sushigo/models.py:65-67. Keeps log-probs/entropy/KL consistent and makes the exported model structurally incapable of proposing an illegal move.
- Weights hot-swap over persistent workers: torch.save(policy) into a BytesIO and push bytes to long-lived actor processes instead of respawning them — chlligence training/self_play_env.py:170-195 + self_play_loop.py:229-244. At 56 actors the respawn cost this avoids is minutes per generation.
- Thread-oversubscription pinning done in the right place: os.environ.setdefault for OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS='1' BEFORE any other import, plus torch.set_num_threads(1) inside each worker — chlligence scripts/train.py:23-25, self_play_env.py:331. 56 actors x 64 cores is 3,584 threads on 64 cores otherwise.
- Paired-seed, side-swapped evaluation: both games of a match pair use the SAME deck seed and differ only in seat assignment; for n>2 rotate through all n seat assignments of one fixed deal — chlligence training/evaluate.py:51-137. Cancels deck-draw variance rather than stacking two independent noisy samples. Also track win rate per seat as a standing seat-asymmetry detector.
- Eval provenance tagging: every rating carries elo_source in {full_eval, incremental, baseline} so a cheap estimate can never later be mistaken for a calibrated measurement — chlligence training/evaluate.py:206-279. Two strings, large payoff in trusting your own logs.
- Observation-encoding version gate: stamp an encoder version into every checkpoint and raise a RuntimeError naming the incompatibility on load mismatch — chlligence training/opponent_pool.py:174-245. Cheap insurance against silently mixing checkpoints trained under different encodings.
- Content-addressed cards with NO card-id embedding: encode every card as [cost vector, reward one-hot, points, tier] — cestpasphoto VectoriseCards / Rinascimento VectoriseCards.java / Splendor-Zero's 11-feature card block. Required for our C5 augmentation to be exact, and it generalizes if the card table is ever rebalanced.
- Relative-cost encoding: feed max(cost - (tokens + discounts), 0) per colour instead of raw cost, plus gold-needed and an affordable flag — BreckEmert deck.py:24-27. The single highest-value feature engineering idea in the profiles; the mask already computes affordability, so give it to the net rather than making it rederive it.
- turns_to_buy = max(ceil(sum(shortfall)/3), max(shortfall)) as an admissible-flavoured distance feature, and the two-level noble distance (sum the gem-distances of the cheapest reachable cards of each colour a tile still needs, charging a max constant for colours with no card on the board) — roeey777 features.py:260-274. Both stay valid under our take rules.
- Exact terminal-value alpha-beta endgame solver with a transposition table and hand-written move ordering (TT move > winning buy > tile > buys > takes) — Splendor-Zero native_endgame.cpp:146. They built it and never wired it in; our return-to-round-leader final round makes it worth wiring.
- Anti-clairvoyance PUCT penalty on RESERVE_FROM_DECK at the root, drawn uniformly from [0, 0.02/0.06/0.12] by tier — Splendor-Zero native_mcts.cpp:547. Targeted mitigation of the determinizer's false certainty about the deck top.
- Search-diagnostic counters as first-class outputs: slots requested / evaluated / dropped-pending / dropped-cycle, plus a leaf-depth histogram — Splendor-Zero native_mcts.h:13-31. Without these, an 'N simulations' claim is unverifiable.
- The 1000-random-game invariant smoke test asserting per step: no negative tokens, nobody above 10 tokens, no negative supply, every game terminates, plus an action-type histogram — chlligence tests/test_env.py. Under our selection-blocking cap the 'never exceeds 10' assertion tests the MASK rather than a discard heuristic, so it is worth more to us than to them.
- Bounded-FIFO frozen-snapshot league with PFSP weights max((1 - winrate_EMA)^p, eps) and unmeasured opponents at max priority — BreckEmert RL/vrpo_league.py:58-115. Use it for the 25% mixed-game slice, sampling each seat independently.
- Rinascimento's 18-event taxonomy (take token / reserve hidden / reserve board / receive tile / receive points ...) as auxiliary prediction targets — game/log/converters/IdentityConverter.java. Dense, cheap, low-dimensional signal for the sparse early phase; their result was that an 18-D trajectory summary beat a 192-D state vector as a rollout evaluator.

### risks
- **AlphaZero cold start.** With a uniform prior and only 32-48 simulations, early Gumbel search barely improves on the prior, and the first few generations can crawl. MITIGATION: the NN-free 2000-sim MCTS bootstrap (3h of CPU, 10M moves) plus n=64 sims for generations 0-3. GO/NO-GO: generation 3 must beat the greedy anchor >=80%.
- **GPU throughput numbers are derived, not measured.** My 1-2.5M evals/s per A100 comes from a FLOP count (2 x 13M x B), not from a benchmark — there is no GPU in this sandbox. If real throughput is 5x lower, we drop to ~180k evals/s per GPU and must either shrink the net, raise the batch, or move a learner GPU to inference. MITIGATION: Phase 4 is a pure throughput benchmark with an explicit numeric gate before any long run.
- **Pure-Python MCTS at 30 us/sim may degrade under real load.** My measurement used a stub evaluator and a single tree; real actors add IPC, serialization, and 24 interleaved trees per process, which will hurt cache locality. If effective throughput falls below ~10k sims/s/core, the numba port of apply/legal_mask/clone (cestpasphoto's flat-int8-array jitclass design) becomes a schedule item, not a contingency. Budget 3-5 days for it.
- **PIMC strategy fusion.** Root determinization assumes each simulation's hidden state is known, which over-values plans that depend on knowing an opponent's hidden reserve or a deck top. In our variant this is mild (no bluffing channel; the unseen multiset is public; deck-reserves are rare) but it is real. MITIGATION: K=16 universes on a shared tree, the deck-reserve PUCT penalty, and a Phase-7 measurement — build a 'clairvoyant' agent that sees the true state and measure the strength gap; if it exceeds ~50 Elo, escalate to true information-set keying (Splendor-Zero's InfoSetKey over an observer-canonical raw state).
- **Rank-based value targets in 3p/4p can encourage second-place play.** A z that rewards rank rather than winning may make the agent settle. MITIGATION: keep the rank target but verify in the arena on WIN RATE, not mean z; if outright wins lag, sharpen the mapping toward winner-take-most.
- **TEAM self-play conventions.** Shared-weight teammates can converge on private protocols that collapse when partnered with a human or a different checkpoint. MITIGATION: 25% of TEAM games draw the two teammate seats independently from the opponent mixture; track 'win rate partnered with a random historical checkpoint' as a standing metric.
- **The stuck terminal may be gameable in the wrong direction.** In TEAM and ONE_V_TWO, deliberately forcing an OPPONENT into a stuck state (denying tokens and board cards) is a legitimate and possibly dominant strategy the agent will discover. That is fine competitively but produces very long, degenerate games. MITIGATION: monitor mean game length and stuck-rate-by-victim per generation; this is a diagnostic to watch, not a bug to suppress.
- **NSCC walltime fragmentation.** ~8-10 chained 24h jobs means checkpoint/resume is on the critical path, and a resume bug silently restarting from generation 0 would be invisible for a day. MITIGATION: resume must be tested by killing and restarting a job in Phase 4; the generation counter and cumulative sample count are logged and asserted monotone.
- **Licensing.** Splendor-Zero, chlligence, seal256, BreckEmert and Nikola995 have NO LICENSE file (all-rights-reserved by default; Splendor-Zero's README claims MIT with no LICENSE present). SIMPLE is GPL-3.0. Only cestpasphoto (MIT, with upstream suragnair attribution) and Rinascimento (MIT) are safe to copy from. MITIGATION: re-implement every idea; copy literal code only from the two MIT repos and attribute both upstream and fork.
- **Gumbel AlphaZero is less battle-tested in hobby code than PUCT.** If the sequential-halving implementation is subtly wrong, training degrades in a way that looks like slow progress rather than a crash. MITIGATION: implement PUCT first as the base path, gate Gumbel behind a flag, and A/B them in Phase 5 with an explicit arena decision; also assert that the improved policy is a valid distribution and that it puts nonzero mass only on legal actions.
- **Encoder/engine drift after the validation gate.** The engine passed 16,000 games with 0 mismatches, but every future edit can break it. MITIGATION: the Node cross-validation runs in CI on every commit touching splendor_ai/rules or the encoder — not once.
- **The 3060 worker is the least-tested component and sits on the critical path to any real strength measurement.** A move that is legal in Python but rejected by the server (e.g. an ENTER_RESERVE expansion edge case) would be discovered only in production. MITIGATION: Phase 9 runs the worker against a LOCAL Node server for >=500 full games in all five modes with a zero-rejection assertion before anything touches Render.

### phase_order
- **P0 — Freeze the decision and the interfaces (0.5 day).** Write docs/AI_DESIGN.md recording this decision, the 65-action table (already fixed), the encoder layout with a version stamp, the terminal-value function per mode, and the actor/learner/inference contract. GO/NO-GO: the encoder spec is complete enough that the network input width is a constant, and every field traces to something view.py already exposes.
- **P1 — Extend the Node cross-validation and make it CI (1 day).** Keep the existing 16,000-game/1.27M-step sweep; ADD targeted corpora for the states random play under-samples: 8/9/10 tokens with partial supply (forced short takes), ENTER_RESERVE with an empty deck and empty face-up row, multi-tile CHOOSE_TILE, TEAM final-round revocation, ONE_V_TWO irrevocable final round, resign/timeout inside the final round, and every is_stuck position reachable in 200k random games. GO/NO-GO: **0 mismatches, two-way legal-set equality, on >=25,000 games across all six configurations, running green in CI.** This gate already passed once — do not let it silently rot.
- **P2 — Encoder + C5 symmetry + baselines (1.5 days).** Implement encode.py (batched, numpy, ~860 floats), the 65-index colour-rotation permutation table, and three fixed anchors: uniform-random-legal, a 1-ply greedy bot, and a NN-free 2000-sim MCTS. GO/NO-GO: (a) for 100k random states and all k in 0..4, `encode(rotate(s,k))` equals `permute(encode(s),k)` exactly and the legal mask permutes correspondingly; (b) the 2000-sim MCTS anchor beats greedy >=85% and greedy beats random >=95% over paired-seed matches in all five modes; (c) encoder throughput >=200k states/s/core.
- **P3 — Network + learner + the arena, offline (1 day).** Build the 13M net, the masked policy head, the four heads, and the Bradley-Terry/Bayes-Elo arena with paired seeds and full seat rotation. Supervised-train on 2M positions from the MCTS anchor. GO/NO-GO: the supervised net alone (no search) beats greedy >=70% and beats random >=98%; policy top-1 agreement with the teacher's argmax >=45%; value sign accuracy >=65%. **If the supervised net cannot beat greedy, the encoder is wrong — stop and fix it before touching self-play.**
- **P4 — Throughput benchmark on the real node (0.5 day, first PBS job).** Stand up 56 actors + 3 inference servers + 1 learner and measure, with no learning: sims/s/core, sims/s node-wide, GPU evals/s per A100 at batch 2048, learner steps/s at batch 4096, and end-to-end self-play moves/s. Kill and restart the job to prove checkpoint/resume. GO/NO-GO: **>=400k sims/s node-wide, >=250k NN evals/s per inference GPU, >=100 learner steps/s, and a clean resume.** If sims/s misses, escalate the numba port BEFORE burning days of self-play; if GPU evals/s misses, shrink the trunk to 512-wide.
- **P5 — Self-play loop, 2p-heavy, with the Gumbel-vs-PUCT A/B (1.5 days).** Bootstrap from P3, run generations 0-10 at n=32-64 on the 2p-heavy mixture. Run both root-selection schemes as parallel arms for the first 5 generations and pick by arena. GO/NO-GO: **by generation 5, >=70% vs the 2000-sim MCTS anchor in 2p; by generation 10, >=85%, with a monotone Elo curve against the FIXED anchors (not against the previous generation).** Also: stuck-rate in self-play must be falling, and search-argmax-differs-from-policy-argmax must be >15% (if it is near zero, search is contributing nothing and something is wrong).
- **P6 — Full five-mode mixture at scale (3 days).** Generations 10-40 at n=48, league mixing on, per-seat independent opponent sampling, pinned anchors. GO/NO-GO at generation 25: **>=90% vs the MCTS anchor in every one of the five configurations; stuck-rate below 2% in every mode; no seat-win-rate asymmetry beyond what the game's structural first-player advantage explains** (measure it against the anchors, which have no seat preference). Abort criterion: if arena Elo against the fixed anchors is flat for 8 consecutive generations, the loop has plateaued — diagnose (replay window, league diversity, sims/move, net capacity) rather than continuing to burn node hours.
- **P7 — Scale-up and the clairvoyance audit (3 days).** Generations 40-70 at n=64-96; optionally widen the trunk with sub-block weight copying. Build a clairvoyant agent that sees the true deck and hidden reserves and measure the Elo gap versus the information-set agent under identical search settings. GO/NO-GO: gap <=50 Elo (PIMC is adequate; proceed); >50 Elo means escalate to information-set tree keying. Also A/B the C5 root ensemble and the exact final-round solver, each of which must show a measurable arena gain to ship.
- **P8 — Per-mode fine-tune and export (1 day).** Fine-tune the shared checkpoint per mode for 6-12h each. GO/NO-GO: a specialist ships only if it beats the shared model >=55% over >=2,000 paired-seed games in its own mode; otherwise ship the shared net for that mode. Export to a single versioned .pt carrying weights + encoder version + config, plus a TorchScript/ONNX path for the worker.
- **P9 — Worker and end-to-end conformance against a LOCAL Node server (1.5 days).** Run the 3060 worker (or a CPU stand-in) against a local server/index.js for >=500 complete games across all five modes, driving both AI and scripted-human seats. GO/NO-GO: **zero rejected actions, zero timeouts at the 2s budget, zero stuck-resignations, p99 move latency <2.0s, and the worker's reconstructed shadow state matching the server's true reserved_public on every step.** Only then point it at Render.
- **P10 — Standing regression harness (ongoing).** Every subsequent checkpoint runs the same anchored arena, the Node cross-validation, and the behaviour diagnostics (game length, cards bought, tiles claimed, gold usage, stuck rate) before it is allowed to replace the deployed model. This is the single practice whose absence made every profiled project's strength claim unverifiable.

### expected_strength
**Stated against fixed anchors, because no profiled project's self-referential Elo means anything.** Targets at P7 completion:

- vs uniform-random-legal: **>99.5%** in all five modes.
- vs the 1-ply greedy bot: **>98%** in all five modes.
- vs the NN-free 2000-sim MCTS anchor: **>=92%** in 2p, **>=85%** in 3p/4p/ovt/team (multi-player win rates compress toward chance, so compare against a 1/n baseline: 85% at 4p against a 25% chance baseline is a very large margin).
- **Search vs no search, same weights**: I expect **+350 to +600 Elo**, bracketing BreckEmert's measured +590 (63%/83%/97% at 25/150/400 sims) and Splendor-Zero's 29-1 result. This is the number to measure first at P7 because it is the cleanest possible ablation and it directly validates the central premise of this recommendation.
- **Deadlock rate**: from the 11-33% I measured under greedy play down to **<0.5%** for the deployed agent (search's 1-ply stuck filter makes it near-zero by construction).
- **Endgame**: provably optimal once the final round is triggered, via the exact determinized solver.

**Versus humans, honestly.** In 2p I expect clearly superhuman play — the position count is small, the branching factor is 8-12, the endgame is solvable, and we will have spent compute comparable to Splendor-Zero's full campaign within 36 hours. In 4p individual and 2v2 the picture is murkier: outcome variance is higher, so even a much stronger agent posts a lower headline win rate, and coordination conventions in 2v2 may not transfer to a human partner. In 1v2 I expect the agent to be strong as the solo (a pure optimization problem) and somewhat weaker as a duo member (implicit coordination against an asymmetric threshold).

**What I am NOT claiming.** No project in the profiles has a credible human benchmark: Splendor-Zero's 2420 rating is 125 games against a field the bot itself filters by rating; BreckEmert's "48-2 on BGA" is self-reported with a population-average screenshot as evidence; the DiVA thesis's "super-human" is a stated aim, not a result. We will be in the same position unless we build the yardstick, which is why the fixed MCTS anchor and an anchored Bayes-Elo ladder are P2/P3 deliverables rather than afterthoughts. The one absolute statement I am comfortable making up front: **a search-equipped agent trained this way will be far stronger than anything reachable by the MaskablePPO configuration in the user-supplied repo**, because that configuration's own checkpoint metadata shows it flat after 51.8M steps.

### disagreements_with_naive_choice
**I disagree with plain MaskablePPO self-play as the main line, on six specific points. Not because PPO is a bad algorithm, but because on this game and this hardware it is the one that leaves the most strength on the table.**

**1. The evidence for it is a measured ceiling, not a starting point.** chlligence's `checkpoints/pool_index.json` records generations 63-99: win rate against the immediately preceding generation oscillating 0.3625-0.6375 around 0.5 (indistinguishable from noise at n=80, sigma ~5.6%), with several late generations measurably *worse* than their predecessor, and Elo wandering inside a ~10-point band — after 51,814,400 environment steps. Their own tooling documents that an earlier, numerically identical-looking `pool_index.json` was produced by broken evaluation code. Treat 50M steps of MaskablePPO on a near-identical card economy as a demonstrated plateau. Scaling the same recipe onto 4xA100 buys more of the same steps, not a different regime.

**2. It cannot use the hardware.** This is the argument I would press hardest. PPO's compute is env stepping (65k plies/s/core here — the CPUs are the work) plus a modest number of gradient steps on a small net. On 4xA100 the GPUs would sit idle >90% of the time; the only lever is a bigger batch, which does not improve a policy. Every profiled project chose PPO or CPU-MCTS *because their env was the bottleneck* — chlligence ran 22 CPU envs with batch-1 opponent forwards, cestpasphoto hardcodes `device='cpu'` and explicitly calls its small-net/many-sims design anti-GPU, Splendor-Zero has zero CUDA in the repo. Our situation is inverted, and AlphaZero is the only candidate that turns idle A100 FLOPs directly into better training targets.

**3. It forfeits the largest single measured effect in the whole landscape.** Search adds roughly +590 Elo on unchanged weights (BreckEmert, same-weights ablation, 150 sims beating the DQN champion 29-1; 97% at 400 sims). Nothing else in any of the ten profiles comes within an order of magnitude of that effect size. A PPO-only pipeline can recover most of it by bolting search on at inference (option 3, the hybrid) — but then it has paid the search cost anyway and forgone the compounding benefit of search-improved *targets* during training. That is the worst of both worlds.

**4. Splendor's decisive skills are lookahead, and our variant makes that sharper.** The hard 10-token cap with no discards creates a genuinely reachable no-legal-move terminal — I measured 12.2/25.5/39.1/42.2% under random play and 18.5/11.3/31.0/33.2% under a greedy bot at 2p/3p/4p/TEAM, driven by token supply being exactly n x 10 at 3p (30) and 4p (40). A stuck seat must resign for score 0. A model-free policy has to amortize avoidance of this into weights; a 1-ply search eliminates it deterministically. The same applies to blocking (Splendor-Zero needed a hand-coded 10x prior boost precisely because their net could not see one-ply threats), to the final-round arithmetic, and to the fewer-cards tiebreak.

**5. Its reward shaping does not survive contact with our five modes.** Making PPO work here means hand-shaping, and chlligence's stack is the template: PBRS + a board-demand vector + a build bonus + a block/restore bonus + a hoarding penalty. Three problems. (a) The hoarding penalty exists ONLY to paper over auto-discard, which our variant does not have — the mask handles the cap. (b) Their PBRS policy-invariance claim is false in their own code: the potential is measured after the agent's move but before the opponent replies, so the telescoping sum does not close, and their `assert gamma == shaping_gamma` gives false confidence about a guarantee that does not hold. (c) Most seriously, their terminal-reward-negation trick depends on Phi being strictly anti-symmetric, which holds for 2 players and symmetric 2v2 but **provably fails for 3-4 player free-for-all** — their own profile flags this. We need 3p and 4p individual and 1v2. AlphaZero needs no potential function, no anti-symmetry, and no zero-sum assumption: just the exact terminal outcome, which our engine already computes.

**6. Its multi-player credit assignment is the weakest part of the recipe, and we need three multi-player modes.** GAE over an interleaved multi-seat trajectory with a terminal-only reward, across 90-110 plies of which only ~25 are yours, is a hard estimation problem — which is exactly why BreckEmert's own author went chasing Q-boosting variants and reported the critic loss "never improving." AlphaZero replaces long-horizon bootstrapping with (search estimate, observed outcome) and a per-seat value vector; the multi-player generalization is a `np.roll` and a max^n backup.

**Where I DO keep PPO, and where I disagree with the current plan's hybrid framing.** `docs/PLAN.md` Sec.4.2 currently makes masked PPO "Level-1 (must succeed)" and search "Level-2 (optional upgrade)". I would invert that priority. Search-in-the-loop is the main line; masked PPO is retained as (a) an *alternative* bootstrap to the NN-free MCTS teacher, (b) a permanent frozen arena baseline, and (c) a pre-built fallback if the AZ loop misses its P5 gate. The infrastructure cost of keeping both is small — identical actors, encoder, network, and arena, differing only in the target-producer module — and it is the right insurance for a one-shot autonomous implementation. But it should be the parachute, not the aircraft.

**Two further disagreements with the plan as written, both cheap to fix:**
- **`docs/PLAN.md` Sec.4.3 specifies a card-id embedding.** Drop it. Content-addressed cards (cost vector, reward one-hot, points, tier) are what make the C5 colour-rotation augmentation exact — an id embedding is not equivariant under the rotation, so it would silently destroy a verified 5x data multiplier and a free test-time ensemble. It also buys nothing: cards are fully characterized by their content.
- **Sec.4.2 and Sec.4.4 propose separate weights per mode and a PBS script that runs four modes on four GPUs in parallel.** That optimizes experiment throughput at the cost of strength: it divides the data five ways and forgoes all transfer. Train one mode-conditioned network on a mixture of all five configurations in a single run, and fine-tune specialists only at the end, only if they win the arena.

```

```markdown
-- algorithm: AlphaZero with KataGo-style additions. All in `MCTS.py` + `Coach.py` + `GenericNNetWrapper.py`.  MCTS (`MCTS.py`): PUCT `u = Qsa + cpuct * Ps[a] * sqrt(Ns)/(1+Nsa)`; unvisited actions get `u = fpu_init + cpuct*Ps[a]*sqrt(Ns+1e-8)` where `fpu_init = Qs - fpu` if fpu>0 (parent-relative reduction) else the absolute value `fpu` (MCTS.py:211-230). Node store is one dict `nodes_data[s] -> (Es, Vs, Ps, Ns, Qsa, Nsa, r, Qs)` keyed by `board.tobytes()` (SplendorGame.py:59-60), i.e. a transposition table reused across moves within an episode, garbage-collected when `round > last_cleaning+20` by deleting nodes with `r < round-5` (MCTS.py:86-91).  Value is a VECTOR of length num_players. `search()` recu
-- rules_fidelity: Standard Splendor, 2/3/4 players. Player count is a MODULE-LEVEL CONSTANT `NUMBER_PLAYERS = 2` at splendor/SplendorGame.py:9 — you edit the source and retrain per player count; it is not a runtime argument.  Faithful to real Splendor AND to our variant on these points (splendor/SplendorLogicNumba.py:140-150, 359-470): - Tokens per color = {2:4, 3:5, 4:7}, gold = 5. Exactly our numbers. - Nobles revealed = {2:3, 3:4, 4:5} = n+1. Exactly our rule. - Noble table (splendor/SplendorLogic.py:127-138): 10 nobles, ALL worth 3 points, 5 of the form 4+4 on two cyclically adjacent colors, 5 of the form 3+3+3 on three cyclically consecutive colors. This is structurally IDENTICAL to our bonus-tile set. -
-- action_space: Fixed 81 actions for all player counts (`action_size()` returns 81, line 94-96). Layout (documented at SplendorLogicNumba.py:53-84, decoded by `move_to_str` in SplendorLogic.py:6-50): - 0-11: buy visible card i (tier = i//4, index = i%4) - 12-23: reserve visible card i - 24-26: reserve blind from deck of tier 0/1/2 - 27-29: buy from own reserve slot 0/1/2 - 30-54: take a combination of 1, 2 or 3 DIFFERENT gems — C(5,1)+C(5,2)+C(5,3) = 5+10+10 = 25 entries, enumerated by `itertools.combinations` in `_gen_list_of_different_gems(3)` - 55-59: take 2 identical gems of color 0..4 - 60-74: give back 1 or 2 different gems (C(5,1)+C(5,2) = 15) - 75-79: give back 2 identical gems of color 0..4 - 80: p
-- network: PyTorch, defined in splendor/SplendorNNet.py; version selected by `-V`. All shipped Splendor checkpoints are `nn_version = 80`.  V80 (shipped): input (B, nb_vect, 7). `LinearNormActivation` (Linear(nb_vect, nb_vect, bias=False) applied on the transposed axis + BatchNorm1d), then ONE `InvertedResidual1d` MobileNetV3 block (expand to 3*nb_vect, "depthwise" Linear(7,7) over the 7-wide axis, Squeeze-Excitation with `_make_divisible(exp//4, 8)` bottleneck, project back, residual). Two separate heads, each = another InvertedResidual1d (Hardswish + max-pool SE) then Flatten -> Linear(nb_vect*7, out) -> ReLU -> Linear(out, out). Policy out = 81; value out = num_players, squashed with `tanh`. Policy 
-- self_play: Vanilla AlphaZero self-play: one network plays every seat. `Coach.executeEpisode` (Coach.py:37-84) canonicalizes, runs `getActionProb(temp=1.)`, samples the move with a decaying temperature, and records (board, pi, curPlayer, valids, q) ONLY when the search was a full one (playout-cap randomization). At game end the reward vector `r` from `check_end_game` is rotated into each sample's own frame via `np.roll(r, -curPlayer)`.  Reward shape: `check_end_game` returns a float32 vector of length n — `+1.0` for the sole winner, `-1.0` for everyone else, or `0.01` for all tied players if the fewer-cards tiebreak fails to separate them. It is NOT zero-sum for n>2 (a 4-player game yields [1,-1,-1,-1])

The `cuda` branch in `switch_target` (lines 292-294) is dead code, reachable only by editing that dict. - Inference is ONNX Runtime with `providers=['CPUExecutionProvider']` and `intra_op_num_threads = inter_op_num_threads = 1` (GenericNNetWrapper.py:326-328). The net is re-exported to ONNX on every mode switch, written to a temp file, loaded, then the file is deleted (`export_and_load_onnx`, lines 300-329). - `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` and `torch.set_num_threads(1)` are

-- algorithm: SEARCH (src/mcts.cpp, 360 lines; mirrored in pysplendor/mcts.py): - Four variants sharing one base: MCTS (plain UCT + random rollout), PolicyMCTS (NN prior, PUCT-style), ValueMCTS (rollout blended with a value fn), PVMCTS (both). Only MCTS and PolicyMCTS are used in the shipped configs. - Nodes store ONLY the action, parent pointer, acting_player, visits, wins, prior p — no game state. Each iteration does `state = root_state->clone()` and replays actions down the path (mcts.cpp:29-33). Deliberate memory/copy tradeoff documented at pysplendor/mcts.py:21-25 ("game states are big, next state computation is relatively cheap"). - Expansion is delayed: a leaf is only expanded on its SECOND visit (
-- rules_fidelity: STANDARD 2-4 player Splendor with a handful of simplifications. Rules live in `SplendorGameRules` (src/splendor.h:94-111 and pysplendor/splendor.py, identical): - num_players 2/3/4; max_open_cards=4; max_hand_cards=3 (reserve limit); win_points=15 (overridable per-run via the `win_points` JSON field — the trained model uses 5); max_player_gems=10; max_nobles = num_players + 1; max_gems_take=3; max_same_gems_take=2; min_same_gems_stack=4; max_gold=5; token stack per color = 7 for 4p, else 2+num_players (4 for 2p, 5 for 3p). - Cards: the real Splendor deck, 40/30/20, hardcoded as strings in src/splendor.cpp:18-22 (also assets/cards.csv, 89 rows + header). Format "[k0|r1g1b2w1]" = black card, 0
-- action_space: Flat, fixed, global action id list of 83 strings (src/splendor.cpp:28-34; mirrored pysplendor/splendor.py:230, PLAYER_ACTIONS_STR at :238): - 1  "s"  — skip (only legal when nothing else is) - 5  "tr2","tg2","tb2","tw2","tk2" — take 2 identical (requires stack >= 4) - 10 "tr1g1b1" ... "tb1w1k1" — take 3 distinct, C(5,3) - 12 "r{level}n{pos}" — reserve face-up card, 3 levels x 4 positions - 12 "p{level}n{pos}" — purchase face-up card - 3  "h0","h1","h2" — purchase from hand (reserved) - 40 "c0".."c39" — CHANCE actions, index into the remaining deck array  => 43 PLAYER actions (network output size, `NUM_ACTIONS = 43` in train.py:17) + 40 chance actions never predicted by the network.  MASKING:
-- network: Tiny MLP, PyTorch, defined in train.py:72-92. - `MLP(input_size=1052, hidden_size=512, hidden_layers=2, out_size=43)`; ReLU; `F.softmax` applied INSIDE forward() (train.py:91) so the exported module emits probabilities. - Parameter count with the shipped defaults: 1052*512+512 = 539,136; 2 x (512*512+512) = 525,312; 512*43+43 = 22,059 → ~1.09M parameters. Roughly 4 MB fp32 — trivially small for a 3060, and far below what 4xA100 could train. - Xavier-uniform init, zero biases. - An alternative `ResNet` (train.py:114-134: initial FC + N residual MLP blocks, final FC zero-initialized) is implemented but commented out at the call site (train.py:264). - NO VALUE HEAD anywhere in the trained pipel
-- self_play: - Pure symmetric self-play: both seats are the SAME current-best model. `_collect_self_play_data` runs best vs best for train (train=True, i.e. sampled root moves) and best vs best for val (train=False, greedy) — self_play.py:132-137. - No league, no opponent pool, no historical-snapshot mixing. The only "opponent diversity" is the 10-iteration replay buffer of past self-play data. - Gated promotion: the freshly trained model plays 1000 games against the current best with `rotate_agents=True`; promoted only if win rate > 0.54 (self_play.py:93, 166-172). Otherwise the best model is kept and an iters_without_improvement counter advances (stop at 12). - Seat handling: `rotate_agents` cyclically
-- distributed: Essentially nothing reusable for a 4xA100 node — this is a single-machine, CPU-thread-parallel design. - Parallelism = `std::async(std::launch::async, ...)` fan-out of `num_workers` threads, each running `num_games/num_workers` complete games sequentially, then a join (src/game.cpp:118-138). Configs use num_workers 9-10 (author's laptop); the shipped self_play_config.json sets num_workers=1. - Remainder games are silently dropped (`num_games / num_workers` integer division). - Reproducibility is explicitly broken under threading: "[warn] do not lead to reproducible games in parallel execution setup (num_workers > 1)" (src/game.h:37). RNG is `std::rand()` seeded once globally (src/main.cpp:44
-- reported_strength: All claims are README-level with modest evidence. Concretely:  BASELINE LADDER (README table, 2-player, 1000 games/pair from baselines.py): - MCTS with unrestricted chance nodes beats Random 0.91 +/- 0.02 → "+400 +/- 40 Elo" - MCTS-500 (max_chance_children=1) beats MCTS-unrestricted 0.89 +/- 0.03 → "+360 +/- 55 Elo" - MCTS-2000 beats MCTS-500 0.66 +/- 0.04 → "+115 +/- 30 Elo" README then says "MCTS is approximately 750 Elo points stronger than a random player (win-points-5 setup, 500 MCTS iterations per move)" — which is the chained sum 400+360, but baselines.py as committed uses GameConfig defaults with win_points=15, so the stated win-points-5 attribution does not match the committed scrip
-- reuse_for_us: DIRECTLY REUSABLE CONCEPTS (re-implement, do not copy, given the missing license):  1. The chance-node contract and the max_chance_children knob. Our variant has three chance sources (face-up refill after buy/reserve, RESERVE_FROM_DECK top card, and the initial deal). Modelling them as explicit CHANCE_PLAYER=-1 nodes in the same GameState interface, then capping children at 1, is the single most transferable idea. Implementation cost: low. But we must NOT copy the backprop reward division (see pitfalls) — pass rewards up unchanged and let visit-count averaging do the expectation.  2. Selection-blocking token cap. seal256 already implements exactly our rule: no discard step, illegal over-cap

Keeps stochasticity out of apply_action and makes the search algorithm game-agnostic. src/game_state.h:29 + src
   * max_chance_children: shuffle a chance node's children then truncate to K (K=1 in every shipped config), turning a ~30-way stochastic branch into a single sampled determinization. src/mcts.cpp:150-153. This is the repo's headline result and the cheapest possible way to keep effective search depth in 
   * Nodes store only the action, not the state; each iteration clones the root state and replays the path down. Combined with a shallow-copy clone (cards are const pointers into immutable static tables) this makes the tree tiny and the copy cost trivial. pysplendor/mcts.py:21-25 (rationale) + src/splend
   * Delay expansion to the second visit of a leaf: the first visit is rollout-only. One line (`node->visits > 0` in the expansion guard, src/mcts.cpp:36) that halves node allocation in a high-branching game.
   * Shuffle children at expansion, then in select_child return the first child with visits==0. Gives random first-play-urgency ordering without any extra RNG in the hot loop. src/mcts.cpp:120-124 + 150.
```

```markdown
-- summary: A small, deliberately generic self-play PPO harness for turn-based multiplayer board/card games. Core idea: a `selfplay_wrapper(env)` mixin converts an N-player Gym env into a *single-agent* env by (a) picking one random seat per episode for the learner, (b) filling all other seats with a frozen checkpoint sampled from a "model bank" on disk, and (c) auto-playing opponents inside `step()` until control returns to the learner, then returning `reward[agent_seat]` as the scalar reward. Six shipped envs: tictactoe (2p), connect4 (2p), sushigo (3p), butterfly (3p), geschenkt (3p, parameterizable), frouge/Flamme Rouge (5p, 2 units each). Stack is TensorFlow 1.15 + stable-baselines 2.10.1 PPO1 + mpi4py (app/requirements.txt) — i.e. no PyTorch, no DDP, no vectorized envs, no GPU batching. The valuable parts for us are architectural patterns, not code: egocentric seat-rotated observations, legal-
-- algorithm: PPO1 from stable-baselines 2.10.1 (`from stable_baselines.ppo1 import PPO1`, app/train.py:16) — the MPI-synchronised, single-env variant of PPO with MpiAdam, NOT PPO2. No MCTS, no search, no value-target bootstrapping tricks, no opponent modelling, no population/league beyond a flat checkpoint list.  Exact defaults from app/train.py:158-177: - gamma 0.99, lam 0.95 (GAE) - clip_param 0.2 - entcoeff 0.1  ← unusually high (10x the typical 0.01); with terminal-only rewards this is the main exploration driver - optim_epochs 4, optim_stepsize 3e-4, optim_batchsize 1024 - timesteps_per_actorbatch 1024 (so batchsize == actorbatch: one minibatch per epoch, per rank) - adam_epsilon 1e-5, schedule 'linear' (LR anneals to 0 over `total_timesteps`) - total_timesteps = int(1e9) with `reset_num_timesteps=False` (train.py:119) — i.e. run forever, kill manually - eval_freq 10240 steps/rank, n_eval_episod

-- algorithm: PPO-Clip, single-episode on-policy, no GAE despite the method name. Entry point `src/splendor/agents/our_agents/ppo/ppo.py::train`; core loop `ppo/training.py`.  Loop shape: for each of MAX_EPISODES=50000 episodes, play ONE full game to termination into a `RolloutBuffer` (capacity 1000), then do PPO_STEPS=10 full-batch gradient steps on that single episode's ~30-100 transitions, then run ONE greedy evaluation game. -- algorithm: No RL. A (1+1) random-mutation hill climber, NOT population-based. The genome is a sequence of *actual Action objects*, each sampled from the state reached by the plan prefix (a_i = rnd(s_t{a_0..a_{i-1}})), not integer indices - this is the key trick for a state-dependent action space. Mutation picks a cut point and RE-ROLLS the whole suffix while replaying the plan. Hyperparameters (class defaults / tuned values): useShiftBuffer, sequenceLength (class default 120, tuned to 2-3), evals (class default 1000, tuned to 200), flipAtLeastOneValue, mutationStyle 0=full-rerandomise / 1=branching
```

```markdown
==============================================================================================================
# petosa/multiplayer-alphazero — "Multiplayer AlphaZero" (Petosa & Balch, NeurIPS 2019 Deep RL Workshop)

## url
https://github.com/petosa/multiplayer-alphazero

## kind
repo + workshop paper (arXiv 1910.13012). Code read in full and cited line-by-line; the paper itself was NOT readable — arxiv.org, ar5iv, arxiv-vanity, deepai, emergentmind, semanticscholar API and news.ycombinator were all EGRESS_BLOCKED, so every paper claim below is from WebSearch snippets and is marked as such.

## summary
The canonical minimal reference implementation of N-player AlphaZero, and the direct ancestor of the "value vector" design our Splendor agent needs. ~1200 lines of Python/PyTorch total. The single idea: replace AlphaZero's scalar value v with a length-N vector v⃗ (one expected utility per seat), have MCTS propagate the whole vector up the path unchanged, and have each node consume only its own mover's component (scores[current_player]) when updating its edge Q. This is exactly MCTS-max^n with a learned prior/value. Terminal states return a score vector ([1,-1,-1] for a P0 win in a 3-player game, [0,0,0] for a draw), and that same vector z⃗ is stamped onto every training position of the game as the value target — no per-player sign flip, no per-player relabelling. Evaluated only on two toy 3-player perfect-information games (Tic-Tac-Mo = 3-player 3x5 tic-tac-toe, and Connect3x3 = 3-player 6x7 connect-3). The mechanism is exactly what we want; the surrounding engineering (batch-1 inference, Python-thread self-play, ~11M-param SENet on a 3x5 board, unbounded replay, no arena gating, no batched leaf evaluation) is toy-scale and should not be copied. Notably the author's *earlier* repo petosa/simple-alpha-zero (Jan 2019) used the naive generalization — scalar v with adj_v = v if current_player == winning_player else -v (simple-alpha-zero/mcts.py:44), i.e. a paranoid "everyone-else-gets--v" backup — and multiplayer-alphazero (Oct 2019) is precisely the fix. That delta is the paper's contribution.

## algorithm
Standard AlphaZero policy-iteration loop, vectorized-ish with numpy, no loops in the selection step.

SEARCH (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-08162026/6c4d3121-5cae-5177-9eec-d5961b7f3014/scratchpad/research/petosa_multiplayer-alphazero/mcts.py, 85 lines):
- Tree is a plain dict keyed by `s.tostring()` (mcts.py:21-22) — a transposition table, no parent pointers. Each entry is an object-dtype array `stats` of shape (num_legal_actions, 4) holding columns [action_index_tuple, N, Q, P] (mcts.py:56-59).
- Selection (mcts.py:32-38): `U = cpuct*P*sqrt(N.sum() + 1e-6)/(1 + N)`; `heuristic = Q + U`; `best_a_idx = np.argmax(heuristic)`. The 1e-6 "epsilon_fix" exists so that U is nonzero when all N=0, letting priors bias the very first visit (mcts.py:26-28). Note this is PUCT with sqrt(sum N) in the numerator, matching AlphaZero.
- Recursion (mcts.py:41-47): apply best action, recurse, then `v = scores[current_player]`, `Q <- (n*q+v)/(n+1)`, `N += 1`, and `return scores` (the FULL vector, untouched).
- Expansion (mcts.py:49-60): terminal check first (`check_game_over(s)` returns None or a score vector); if terminal return the score vector without inserting into the tree, so terminals are re-evaluated cheaply on every visit. Otherwise one NN forward pass, store priors P over the legal actions only, return v⃗.
- `get_distribution(s, temperature)` (mcts.py:65-83): π ∝ N^(1/T), with T→0 handled as argmax via the ZeroDivisionError/OverflowError catch, and a uniform fallback when every child is unvisited.

SELF-PLAY (trainer.py:26-69): one persistent MCTS tree per game (tree reused across moves within a game, never pruned); num_simulations per move; sample action from π; append [s, π, None]; at game end, `for i: data[i][-1] = scores` (trainer.py:66-67).

TRAINING (neural_network.py:24-37, 52-69): `train()` draws ONE minibatch of 64 with replacement from the whole buffer and takes ONE Adam step; `policy_iteration` calls it num_updates (=1000) times. Loss = `p_loss + v_loss` where `v_loss = ((v_pred - v_gt)**2).sum()` (neural_network.py:59) and p_loss is a Python for-loop over the batch computing -sum(π_gt * log_softmax(masked logits)) (neural_network.py:60-68). Legal-action masking is done with `torch.masked_select` on a boolean mask then log_softmax over only the valid entries (neural_network.py:73-81) — the same variable-length-legal-set trick we need for Splendor's 65-action space.

NETWORK (models/senet.py): pre-activation SE-ResNet, blocks [2,2,2,2], planes 64/128/256/512, global avg pool, then `p_head = Linear(512, prod(p_shape))` and `v_head = Linear(512, prod(v_shape))` with `v = torch.tanh(...)` (senet.py:91-92, 118-119). ~11.26M params per the author's own project page. models/senetbig.py is the same with blocks [3,4,6,3].

NO arena/gating: main.py:46-62 always trains on the newest net and checkpoints every `ckpt_frequency` iterations; `rank_checkpoints`/`one_vs_all` in experiments.py are post-hoc analysis, not a promotion gate.

## multiplayer_handling
THE CORE MECHANISM, exactly as implemented.

1) VALUE HEAD SHAPE. `v_shape = (game.get_num_players(),)` (neural_network.py:13) is passed into the model constructor; SENet emits `v = tanh(Linear(512, N)).view(batch, N)` (senet.py:92, 119). N independent tanh outputs in [-1,1]. There is NO softmax, NO sum-to-zero and NO sum-to-one constraint across the N components. Nothing in the algorithm requires zero-sum — which matters for us, see below.

2) SEAT INDEXING IS ABSOLUTE, NOT RELATIVE. v⃗[i] is "expected final score of seat i", in fixed seat order. The network is NOT given a canonicalized/rotated state; instead the whose-turn-it-is information is fed as N one-hot planes broadcast over the board (games/tictacmo.py:13-14 builds a 3x5x(3+3) tensor; take_action flips the indicator planes at tictacmo.py:26-28; get_player reads them back at tictacmo.py:46-48). Consequence: the net must learn seat symmetry from scratch, and there is no N-fold data amplification from rotating seats.

3) TERMINAL SCORE VECTORS. `check_game_over` returns None when the game is live, else a numpy vector indexed by player (game.py:16-21). Concretely (games/tictacmo.py:33-43): `reward = -np.ones(3); reward[p] = 1` → a P1 win is [-1,1,-1]; a full board is `np.zeros(3)` = [0,0,0]. Note these sum to -1, not 0 — the implementation is NOT zero-sum-constrained and does not care.

4) BACKUP (the whole trick), mcts.py:42-47:
       scores = self.simulate(s_prime)         # full length-N vector comes back
       v = scores[current_player]              # "Index in to find our reward"
       stats[best_a_idx, 2] = (n*q + v)/(n + 1)  # running mean Q for THIS edge
       stats[best_a_idx, 1] += 1
       return scores                           # vector passed up UNCHANGED
   `current_player = self.game.get_player(s)` (mcts.py:31) is the player to move at the PARENT node s, i.e. the owner of the edge being updated. So each node's Q column is measured in the currency of the player who moves at that node, and since selection is `argmax(Q + U)` over that node's own stats, every node greedily maximizes its own mover's component. That is textbook max^n / MCTS-max^n, and it drops out of two lines. No sign flipping anywhere; the vector is never negated, permuted or rescaled on the way up. Only ONE component of the vector is consumed per level — the rest are carried so ancestors can consume theirs.

5) TRAINING TARGET. trainer.py:66-67: the SAME final score vector z⃗ is written into every training row of the game, regardless of who was to move. Tuples are (s_i, π⃗_i, z⃗) — matching the paper's notation "(s_i, π⃗_i, z⃗) tuples since value is a vector" (WebSearch snippet). Combined with the absolute seat indexing and the turn planes in s, this is self-consistent: the net learns "given this board and whose turn it is, what does each seat finally score".

6) N-PLAYER TURN ROTATION. Handled purely inside each Game: `s[:,:,num_p+p] = 0; s[:,:,num_p+(p+1)%num_p] = 1` (tictacmo.py:27-28, connect3x3.py:32-33). MCTS is player-count-agnostic.

7) EVALUATION UNDER SEAT ASYMMETRY. play.py:8-38 with `permute=True` plays every permutation of the seat assignment (3! = 6 games per "match" for 3 players) and accumulates `scores[list(order)] += game_over`, so first/second/third-mover advantage is cancelled. experiments.py:15-22 pits one DeepMCTSPlayer against (N-1) UninformedMCTSPlayers at doubling strengths 10,20,...,1280 (main.py:60-62). Paper snippet confirms: "a total of 6 games is played between the same opponents — one game for each permutation of players to break any advantages from going first, second, or third."

8) TEAMS / CREDIT ASSIGNMENT: ABSENT. Zero support — grep for team/coalition/cooperative finds nothing. Every seat is an independent maximizer. There is also no backup rule variant (no paranoid, no offensive, no BRS, no mixing), no opponent modelling, and no tie-break policy when several actions share max heuristic beyond numpy's first-index argmax.

## hidden_info_handling
NONE, at every level, and it is not a small gap.

- game.py declares a fully-observable API: `get_initial_state()` returns THE state, `get_available_actions(s)`, `check_game_over(s)`, `take_action(s,a)`, `get_player(s)`. There is no information-set concept, no per-player observation function, no chance/nature node, no determinization, no belief state, no sampling of unknowns. Grep for hidden/imperfect/belief/determiniz/chance/stochast over the whole repo: zero hits.
- MCTS keys nodes on the raw full state bytes (`s.tostring()`, mcts.py:22), so a node IS a world state, not an information set. Two histories that are indistinguishable to the mover are still distinct search nodes only if the ground truth differs — and the search happily reads the ground truth when expanding.
- The network is fed the same full state s that the search uses, so an agent built this way would peek at the opponent's private information.
- The paper (per WebSearch snippets of the abstract) explicitly scopes itself to "two-player, deterministic, zero-sum games where perfect information of the game state is available" and generalizes only the player-count axis; it says nothing about imperfect information. I could not open the PDF to check the future-work section, so I cannot claim it discusses hidden information at all.

For our Splendor variant this means the repo answers our value-vector question completely and our hidden-info question not at all. Our two hidden components — deck order (a chance/nature source) and opponents' deck-reserved cards (private state) — need machinery from elsewhere (determinization/IS-MCTS, or the far simpler and probably right first move: treat the deck as a stochastic environment by shuffling a consistent deck at the root of each self-play game and giving the network only the acting seat's legal observation, i.e. train a "perfect-recall-of-my-own-info" net rather than a cheating net). Nothing in this repo helps you do that; copying its Game interface verbatim will silently build a cheating agent.

## training_recipe
CODE-VERIFIED (configs/tictacmo-gpu.json, configs/connect3x3-gpu.json, configs/tictactoe-gpu.json — all three are byte-identical apart from the game name and ckpt_frequency, so "the same hyperparameters are used across all games and experiments"):
- num_simulations (MCTS rollouts per move): 50. Same 50 at train time and at eval time.
- cpuct: 3.
- num_games (self-play games per policy iteration): 30.
- num_updates (Adam steps per policy iteration): 1000, each on a batch of 64 sampled WITH REPLACEMENT from the whole buffer (neural_network.py:27-28). So 64,000 sample-draws per iteration off ~30 games.
- batch_size: 64. lr: 1e-3, Adam. weight_decay: 1e-4 (coupled L2 inside Adam, not AdamW).
- buffer_size_limit: null in every config → UNBOUNDED replay buffer, never pruned (trainer.py:95-96 is a no-op).
- temperature: hard-coded 1 for the entire game, never annealed (trainer.py:75). Deviates from AlphaZero's T=1 for the first ~30 plies then T→0.
- Dirichlet noise: alpha=1, weight=0.25, applied at the FIRST MOVE OF THE GAME ONLY (trainer.py:33-34, 44-48 — `root` is set True once before the while loop and set False after the first move), and applied to the post-search visit distribution which is then ALSO stored as the policy target (trainer.py:47 then :50). AlphaZero instead adds noise to the root priors P before every move's search. Both the "once per game" and the "contaminates the label" parts are deviations.
- num_threads: 1 in the GPU configs; when >1, self-play games are farmed to `multiprocessing.dummy.Pool` (trainer.py:3, 80-86) — Python threads, GIL-bound, one independent tree each, shared NN.
- Inference: `predict` wraps a single state as `np.array([s])` (neural_network.py:43) — batch size 1 per simulation. No leaf batching, no virtual loss, no inference server.
- cuda: true wraps the model in `torch.nn.DataParallel` (neural_network.py:16-18), which is useless at batch 1.
- ckpt_frequency: 1 for TicTacMo/TicTacToe, 5 for Connect3x3. Evaluation after each checkpoint against uninformed MCTS at strengths 10,20,40,80,160,320,640,1280 (main.py:60-62).
- Network: SENet, PreActBlock [2,2,2,2], 64→128→256→512 planes, ~11.26M params. On a 3x5 board three stride-2 stages take 3x5 → 2x3 → 1x2 → 1x1 before the heads — extremely aggressive downsampling for a tiny board.

PAPER-REPORTED, SNIPPET-ONLY (arXiv PDF blocked — treat as low-confidence, single-source paraphrase):
- Training wall-clock: "about 18 hours" of self-play for Tic-Tac-Mo, and separately "about 18 hours" for Connect 3x3. No hardware named in any snippet I could retrieve, no iteration count, no sample count.
- Loss: "sum of cross-entropy loss and mean squared error", value head tanh in [-1,+1] — consistent with the code.
- No learning-rate schedule, no gating, no data augmentation (no board symmetries) appear anywhere in the code, and no snippet mentions any.

## reported_strength
All strength claims below come from WebSearch snippets of arXiv 1910.13012 — I could NOT open the PDF or any HTML mirror, so I have no tables, no figures and no error bars. Evidence quality: MEDIUM for the qualitative claims (they were returned consistently across several independent queries), LOW for anything numeric.

- Abstract (retrieved verbatim, high confidence): "we suggest novel modifications of the AlphaZero algorithm to support multiplayer environments, and evaluate the approach in two simple 3-player games. Our experiments show that multiplayer AlphaZero learns successfully and consistently outperforms a competing approach: Monte Carlo tree search."
- Tic-Tac-Mo: "suffered no defeats against computer or human opponents." "With just 50 rollouts, AlphaZero had equivalent performance to at least a 3000-rollout MCTS and could pick a move in a fraction of the time." So the headline is roughly a 60x search-efficiency multiplier on a 15-cell 3-player game.
- Protocol: AlphaZero is held at a fixed 50 rollouts while the MCTS opponents' rollouts are doubled match over match; each match is 6 games (all 3! seat permutations). Figure 3(a) plots AlphaZero score vs MCTS score per match; 3(b) plots the same for a 50-rollout vanilla-MCTS control. "AlphaZero convincingly defeats MCTS agents that have few rollouts, but score starts to converge as MCTS strength increases", and "the AlphaZero control mostly beat stronger MCTS agents while maintaining a non-negative score."
- Connect 3x3 (the harder game, 42 plies): "results from Connect 3x3 indicate that the overall multiplayer AlphaZero strategy works, but more hyperparameter tuning is needed to truly master complex games." I.e. honest partial success, not mastery.
- Calibration for us: these are 15-cell and 42-cell games with 15 and 7 actions respectively, trained for 18 hours at 50 sims. Splendor with a 65-action space, ~40-80 plies, hidden info and four game modes is one to two orders of magnitude harder. Do not read "no defeats" as evidence the recipe scales.
- The author's own predecessor project page (petosa/simple-alpha-zero/project_webpage/index.html, 2-player games, read locally in full) gives the only real numbers I could verify: average win rate vs a ladder of vanilla-MCTS opponents (10 → 20,480 iters) — Tic-Tac-Toe: UCT control 0.396, MLP 0.542, MiniVGG 0.667, SENet 0.667; Connect-4: control 0.292, MLP 0.771, MiniVGG 0.750, SENet 0.771. Also candid negatives: on Connect-4 "for each of the networks, there is a match our win rate hits 0% — if our agents were playing optimally, this would never happen", and the shallower nets' training loss actually diverged while generalizing just as well as SENet.

## reuse_for_us
Adopt the MECHANISM verbatim; discard the engineering. Concretely for the Splendor variant:

1) VALUE HEAD = length-N vector, tanh, no normalization across components. Ship one head sized to the max seat count (4) and mask/ignore unused seats, or instantiate per mode. The repo proves no zero-sum constraint is needed — which is exactly what our modes require, because "winner by excess" (1v2) and "team total > 30 plus second-score condition" (2v2) are not naturally zero-sum. Use continuous z in [-1,1] (e.g. tanh-squashed margin) rather than only ±1: the tanh head and the MSE loss support it unchanged, and it gives dense signal for the excess-based win conditions.

2) BACKUP = the two lines from mcts.py:44-47. Return the full vector, consume `scores[current_player]` at each node, never negate. This is the whole answer to "how do 3- and 4-player Splendor seats back up value".

3) TEAMS FALL OUT FOR FREE — this is the extension the repo doesn't make but is trivially implied. Keep the vector indexed by SEAT (length 4), and define z per seat as that seat's TEAM outcome:
   - 2v2: z = [T_A, T_B, T_A, T_B] (or whatever the seat→team map is). Then `scores[current_player]` at a node owned by a team-A seat already equals the team-A value, so both A seats maximize the same quantity and the max^n backup becomes cooperative with ZERO code change.
   - 1v2: z = [solo, duo, duo]. Same argument; the AI can be trained as the solo seat and as a duo member from the same net.
   - 2p / 3p / 4p individual: z = per-seat result.
   Do NOT collapse the vector to a length-2 "team value" — keeping it seat-indexed lets one net serve all four target agents and keeps the indexing identical to the repo's.

4) LEGAL-ACTION MASKING: copy `get_valid_dist` (neural_network.py:73-81) semantically — log_softmax over the legal subset only, for BOTH the prediction and the loss — but vectorize it. The repo's Python for-loop over the batch (neural_network.py:60-68) is fine at 15 actions and will dominate our step time at 65 actions × batch 1024. Use a fixed 65-wide logit tensor, add -1e9 at illegal positions, one batched log_softmax, and a masked KL. Same math, ~100x faster.

5) SEAT CANONICALIZATION — DEVIATE. The repo uses absolute seat order plus turn-indicator planes. For us, rotate the observation so the acting seat is index 0 and emit the value vector in ROTATED order; this gives an N-fold effective data multiplier and removes the seat-symmetry learning burden. Caveat specific to our rules: our seats are NOT interchangeable (1v2 solo is always seat 0 and always starts; the individual-mode tiebreak and the "final round ends when turn returns to the first player" rule privilege earlier seats), so keep an explicit "turn-order position" and "seats remaining this round" feature after rotating, and do not rotate across the solo/duo boundary in 1v2.

6) EVALUATION: steal play.py's `permute=True` seat-permutation match (play.py:11, 17, 33) wholesale — for 4-player that is 24 games per match, which is affordable and is the right way to kill seat bias in our asymmetric modes. Steal experiments.py's doubling-strength ladder (10→1280) against a search-only baseline as the primary "is it learning" curve; it needs no reference agent and is mode-agnostic.

7) UNIT-TEST IDEA FROM THE SIBLING REPO: petosa/simple-alpha-zero/tests/mcts_tests.py builds deliberately trivial games (OnePlayerGuessIt 2x2, TwoPlayerGuessIt, ThreePlayerLinearLeapFrog) whose search trees can be worked out by hand, then asserts the exact (N, Q, P) triple on every edge after each individual simulation. Build a "MiniSplendor" with a handful of actions and do the same — it is the only cheap way to prove the max^n backup and the 65-action mask are bit-correct before burning A100-hours.

8) THROUGHPUT — REPLACE ENTIRELY. batch-1 predict + GIL-bound thread pool + 11M-param SENet will not give us 2 s/move on a 4GB RTX 3060. For inference: small MLP/ResNet over a flat feature vector (Splendor has no meaningful 2D spatial structure — a conv tower is the wrong prior here), leaf-batched MCTS with virtual loss, fp16, target 400-800 sims in the 2 s budget. For training: 4xA100 DDP with a proper actor pool writing to a bounded replay buffer, not `np.concatenate` on an object array every iteration.

## ideas_to_steal
- The two-line max^n backup: return the full length-N score vector up the recursion untouched and consume only scores[current_player] into the edge Q (mcts.py:42-47). Player-count-agnostic, no sign flips, no special cases — this is the whole multiplayer contribution and it is 3 lines of code.
- One shared z⃗ target for every position in a game (trainer.py:66-67): the (s_i, π⃗_i, z⃗) tuple. No per-player relabelling, no separate nets per seat — one network serves every seat, which is exactly what we need for 2p/3p/4p/1v2/2v2 from one model.
- Nothing in the scheme requires zero-sum: terminal vectors in the repo sum to -1 for 3 players and it works fine. So our 'winner by excess' and team-total conditions can be encoded as continuous per-seat utilities in [-1,1] with no algorithmic change.
- Teams need zero new machinery — just set z_i to seat i's TEAM outcome and the max^n backup becomes cooperative automatically, because scores[current_player] is already the team value for every seat on that team. This is the natural extension to our 2v2 and 1v2 modes.
- Masked log_softmax over only the legal action subset, applied identically in predict and in the loss (neural_network.py:73-81) — the right pattern for our 65-action space where most actions are illegal most of the time.
- The epsilon_fix: sqrt(sum(N) + 1e-6) so U is nonzero at N=0 and priors bias the very first visit to a node (mcts.py:26-28, 35). Small, cheap, and meaningfully helps when the prior is good — relevant to us because a Splendor prior over 65 mostly-illegal actions is very informative.
- Seat-permutation matches (play.py:11,17,33) as the standard evaluation unit — play all n! seat orderings and sum, so first-mover advantage cannot flatter the agent. Mandatory for our seat-asymmetric modes.
- The doubling-strength search-only ladder (10,20,...,1280 sims) as a reference-free strength curve, plus a same-budget search-only control agent on the same ladder to isolate 'what did the network actually buy me' (experiments.py:15-22, 72-93, main.py:60-62).
- Terminal nodes are evaluated but never inserted into the tree (mcts.py:50-52) — they get re-derived on each visit, which keeps the transposition table clean and avoids stale terminal stats.
- From the sibling repo petosa/simple-alpha-zero: hand-computable toy games (2x2 'guess-it', 3-player 'leapfrog') with unit tests asserting exact per-edge (N,Q,P) after each individual simulation (tests/mcts_tests.py). Build the Splendor equivalent before scaling.

## pitfalls
- cpuct is NOT propagated into the recursion. mcts.py:42 calls `self.simulate(s_prime)` with no cpuct argument, so the configured cpuct=3 applies only at the root of each simulation and every deeper node silently uses the default cpuct=1. All published results were produced with this inconsistency. Pass it (or make it an attribute) in our port.
- Dirichlet noise is applied only at the FIRST move of each game, not at the root of every move (trainer.py:33-34, 44-48 — `root` is set False after one move), and it is added to the post-search visit distribution which is then stored AS THE POLICY TARGET (trainer.py:47 then :50) rather than to the root priors P before search. So it neither shapes the search nor stays out of the labels. Do it properly: perturb P at the root of every move's search.
- Dirichlet alpha=1 is a flat Dirichlet, not the spiky alpha<1 (0.03-0.3) AlphaZero uses; combined with weight 0.25 this is closer to uniform label smoothing than to targeted exploration.
- The value loss is `((v_pred - v_gt)**2).sum()` (neural_network.py:59) — summed over batch AND over the N value components, while the policy loss is summed over batch only. So the value:policy weighting silently scales with player count: our 4-player and 2v2 nets would get 2x the relative value weight of a 2-player net at the same batch size. Normalize by batch and by N, or weight explicitly.
- The logged training error is wrong. trainer.py:109 computes `(mean_loss*count + new_loss)/(count+1)` and DISCARDS the result — mean_loss is set once on the first update and never changed, so error_log records the loss of the first minibatch of each iteration, not the mean over 1000 updates. Every 'loss decreases and stabilizes' claim rests on this statistic.
- Q is initialized to 0 for unvisited edges (mcts.py:56 zeros). In an N-player game the typical terminal vector is [1,-1,...,-1], so a seat's expected value is strongly negative; Q=0 is therefore systematically optimistic and biases the search toward unvisited actions in a way that gets worse as N grows. Consider first-play-urgency (init Q to the parent's value) instead.
- A state with NO legal actions crashes. `idx = np.stack(np.where(available))` gives an empty (0,k) array, stats becomes shape (0,4), and the next selection visit hits `np.argmax` on an empty array → ValueError (mcts.py:34-37, 53-59). Our Splendor has exactly this case (10 tokens, 3 reserved, nothing affordable). We must define an explicit pass/no-op action in the 65-action space rather than an empty legal set.
- Absolute (non-canonicalized) seat indexing plus turn-indicator planes means the network must learn seat symmetry from data, forfeiting an N-fold data multiplier. Fine for 3-player tic-tac-toe with 18h of self-play; expensive for us.
- The MCTS tree is never pruned or re-rooted between moves within a game (trainer.py:28 creates it once) and the transposition dict keys on full state bytes — memory grows monotonically over a game and across a whole match for DeepMCTSPlayer (reset only between matches, players/deep_mcts_player.py:27-28). With Splendor's much larger state and longer games this is a real leak.
- Batch-1 inference (neural_network.py:43) inside a per-simulation Python recursion, with `DataParallel` wrapping (neural_network.py:16-18) that can never fill. Self-play parallelism is `multiprocessing.dummy` = GIL-bound threads (trainer.py:3, 80-86), and the GPU configs set num_threads=1 anyway. There is no virtual loss, no leaf batching, no inference server — this is the single biggest thing that will not scale to our 4xA100 training or 2 s/move 3060 inference.
- Unbounded replay buffer (buffer_size_limit: null in all three configs) with 1000 Adam steps x batch 64 = 64,000 draws per iteration off ~30 games (~360 positions for Tic-Tac-Mo). Extreme sample reuse and near-certain overfitting in early iterations; also `np.concatenate` on an object-dtype array every iteration is O(buffer) per iteration.
- Temperature is hard-coded to 1 for the entire game (trainer.py:75), never annealed toward 0 in the endgame — so late-game self-play moves stay noisy and the value targets are correspondingly noisier.
- No arena / no gating: main.py always continues from the newest net. Combined with an unbounded buffer this can absorb a regression silently; `rank_checkpoints` (experiments.py:26-48) is only run by hand afterwards.
- No board-symmetry augmentation anywhere, despite tic-tac-toe-family games having 8-fold dihedral symmetry. (Not applicable to Splendor, but it means the reported sample efficiency is not a tuned upper bound.)
- The code will not run on a modern stack as-is: `np.object` (mcts.py:56, games/*.py), `np.float`/`np.bool` (trainer.py:53, simple-alpha-zero games), and `ndarray.tostring()` (mcts.py:22) were all removed in NumPy >= 1.24. Use `.tobytes()` and explicit dtypes.
- Evidence limits: the arXiv paper itself is unreadable from this environment (arxiv.org, ar5iv, arxiv-vanity, deepai, emergentmind, semanticscholar API, HN all EGRESS_BLOCKED). Every strength number above is a WebSearch snippet paraphrase with no table, no variance and no hardware spec. Do not cite '50 rollouts ≈ 3000-rollout MCTS' as a measured result without opening the PDF elsewhere.
- Scope mismatch: two toy 3-player perfect-information games, 15 and 7 actions, ~15 and ~42 plies, 18h of training. Nothing here validates the approach at Splendor's action-space size, horizon, hidden information, or team structure.
```
